restrictions: Messages of 55 and 63 bytes (the 63-byte one ends in eight zero bytes): one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and the true block length; unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision of two distinct complete messages.

Construction, constants, class of Y4, rule A and Lemma N are from submission c66f230d (Jbenisek, co-author tekkac); lanes from ticket 2bf40fb (tekkac); complement propagation follows 8c81a219 (Th0rgal); Jbenisek, tekkac and Th0rgal are co-authors. New: the sub-class S8 (65,536 members), the member order, the beta filter (Lemma B), Lemmas D and D', the branch-free 64-register counted batch that computes the full residual of every trial, and the block accumulator.

Exact part: for every eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7 (Theorem 1), with Y4 in S8, and the packed batch computes the XOR differences of digest words 1, 3, 4 and 6 exactly (Lemma D). Heuristic part: a search over N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 = 2^100.53 such pairs, each computed to its 128-bit residual (four words equivalent to it, Lemma D') and tested against zero; success needs one trial with R = 0, and H1 counts only those that also satisfy rule A and the beta filter.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers; seven trials per word in 36-bit lanes; every batch executes the same 219 operations (no stages, no budgets) and ANDs a per-lane zero indicator into a block accumulator tested once per X14 value, plus loop and per-X14 set-up: 31.2987 counted, 31.30 charged per trial, every executed primitive including loads counted as 1; step 3 runs at most once; no sorting, lookup or growing table. The time bound holds for every value of the coins.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word. Success probability 0.39 holds only under H1, the only heuristic. The factor F = 92,675,072 = 2^26.4657 in H1 is assumed; it is half of an exact model count of 185,350,144 (margin 2.000), recomputed by the shipped program's --count mode, that the organizer experiments do not measure. With the uniform rate the same search gives 123.22. No full collision is exhibited.

Preprocessing: a declared charge of 2^86 units (2^94.75 word operations) covers all selection of the stored constants, class, rule A, sub-class and filter by c66f230d and by us, without reliance on run records (more than 2^34 times c66f230d's own estimate). Memory 2^100 bytes bounds that preprocessing by its charged work; the search itself uses under 2^21 bytes. Advice under 64 bytes.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the N = 1,512,538 * 2^80 trials of proof.md Section 4 behave, with respect to the event good (128-bit residual R = 0, rule A, and E1's c1 passes the beta filter), like independent events of probability at least F * 2^-128 each (F = 92,675,072 = 185,350,144 / 2 = 2^26.4657), to the extent that the probability that no trial is good is at most exp(-lambda) + 0.002 with lambda = N * F * 2^-128 = 0.4980001.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Fact P, Y4 in the sub-class S8 of Section 3 (all 65,536 members per context, in the stated order), contexts with four words from the random word, vc over 2^32 values, vd below 1,512,538 and X14 over 2^32 values; rule A as in Lemma A; the filter (c1 AND 00098188) = 00008000.
heuristics.extrapolation: From an exact count under the seven-word model M (proof.md Section 8): restricted to the six betas of T6, which the filter contains by Lemma B, the share of solutions of R = 0 with rule A among Y4 in S8 times 2^192 is 185,350,144 * 2^-128, an exact integer from 57 nonzero of 85 outcomes counted by carry automata in exact integer arithmetic without sampling (equal with and without rule A). The shipped program recomputes it: python3 experiments/s8search.py --count prints N1, N3 and the part of every outcome, the six per-beta parts and the total (about 2.5 minutes). Our C counter, this Python port and a separately written counter (183,119,872 for the four heaviest betas) agree exactly; a sampling estimator by our review agent gives ratio 1.0007 +- 0.0047; every member of S8 has an exact factor of at least 184.57M (all 15 betas); the full-class parts equal the published table of c66f230d; brute force at 8-bit words agrees on every outcome, member split and rule split. On real trials, rule-A and filter rates agree with the model at rates 2^-5 to 2^-11, the E1 part has real/model 1.0086 over 2^33.8 trials, and E3 partial events of probability about 2^-38 show the counter's S8-versus-rest ratios (1, 2.333, 7) on real trials as on model draws. The claimed factor F is exactly half of the count. The extrapolation is from the model count and these checks to the rate of good trials among 2^100.53 real trials.
heuristics.limitations: The factor is assumed, set at exactly half of a model count that organizer experiments do not measure (margin 2.000). M is untested at probability 2^-100.5; real trials were compared with it for events down to about 2^-38 per trial here (E1 part, E3 partial events) and about 2^-40 for one call in c66f230d; the full E3 event has too few hits at our sample size to test (real 0.80 +- 0.20, model draws 0.51 +- 0.15 with the same estimator). M fails inside one context for rule A; only averages over contexts are measured. The constants, class and rule A were chosen by c66f230d to maximize a count of this kind; S8 is the best under M of 8,992,320 sub-classes given by three one- or two-bit conditions on e1 and supplies a factor 1.29 of the margin (if its advantage under M were entirely a selection artifact, S8 trials would have the class rate, and the full class with rule A counts 1.555 F >= F); the filter was chosen to contain the heaviest betas; choices that are best under M may favour parameters where M overstates. 37% of the S8 count (44% in the full class) comes from one beta, 18b0e098. Trials of a run share four seed words and trials of one context differ only in Y4; their independence is assumed. The count program runs on the participant side (about 2.5 minutes), not as an organizer experiment. Run selection: no organizer-run count or frequency supports F; the experiments' predictions are exact per-seed predicates, every recorded replay of this version is reported (proof.md Section 6: 41 runs with nonces fixed before running, 44 earlier ones), and no parameter, version, seed or nonce was chosen on replay outcomes.
